Garnet v0.8.3 is a research-grade (v0.x) release, not production or 1.0. The full record is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://garnet-lang.org/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell: `irm https://garnet-lang.org/install.ps1 | iex`.

When `gpg` is installed, both installers check that `SHA256SUMS` is signed by the release key they pin for v0.8.3, and stop if it is not. Without `gpg` they warn and check integrity only.

## What changed since v0.8.2

- **Linux packages for older distributions.** The x86_64 and ARM64 `.deb`, `.rpm` and tarballs are built on Ubuntu 22.04 under a `GLIBC_2.34` floor and installed in clean Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 and AlmaLinux 9 containers in CI.
- **Signature-checking installers.** `install.sh` and `install.ps1` verify `SHA256SUMS.asc` against the pinned key before they trust any checksum.
- **A converter whose output parses.** Every file `garnet convert` writes parses as Garnet; constructs it cannot map become `@migrate_todo` comments carrying their source.
- **Capability checking.** More host primitives are gated by `@caps` at run time, memory declarations sit under a `mem` capability, and the checker reports capabilities reached through call-graph cycles. Per-function names carry their module path, so `diff-caps` no longer merges same-named functions.
- **Truthful tools.** `garnet agent-loop` says the program-wide surface did not widen and lists per-function changes for review; `garnet caps-log` refuses to overwrite a log it cannot read.

## Verify

`SHA256SUMS` is signed with the release key listed in [docs/release-signing.md](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/docs/release-signing.md), which also gives the commands. The keys are in [docs/garnet-release-keys.asc](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/docs/garnet-release-keys.asc):

```sh
gpg --import garnet-release-keys.asc
gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
```

## Limits

- Only `@caps` and `@max_depth` trap at run time. `@bounded` step budgets, memory and time ceilings, `@mailbox`, and OS-sandbox application on macOS and Windows are declared, not enforced; seccomp is applied on Linux only.
- The Rust and Go converter frontends drop binary operators, so their output parses but does not compute the same thing.
- WV-6 (native-Windows acceptance) is a disclosed partial.
- The binaries are not code-signed. Garnet Studio is not a release asset.
